data.content_ref: inline:The preference is justified not by looking backward at survival rates but forward at informational content and verisimilitude (truth-likeness). Severe tests target high-content theories; surviving them suggests the theory captures more structural reality than a refuted rival, even if we cannot assign a probability to this capture. We choose the better-corroborated theory because it is our best current guess at being closer to the truth, not because it is statistically safer. This costs us the ability to quantify 'closeness to truth' precisely, forcing science to remain a qualitative journey toward an unreachable horizon.
